messages:
Priya: Quick Q about the rerank endpoint contract — trying to lock down tie-break semantics and which score clients should treat as the canonical ranking signal. cc @Tom @Nadia :eyes:
Tom: Re: tie-break — I think we currently fall back to input order but that was never documented. We should be explicit. Also need to decide what 'score' means: raw model output vs normalized rank score.
Nadia: Agreed. Implementation note: models produce a raw relevance value (could be logits or similarity) we call 'score' today. But for stable client behaviour we want to add a normalized 'rank_score' in [0,1]. Backwards compatible path possible.
Priya: Are we comfortable with adding fields rather than changing 'score'? Adding is safest. What's the plan for pagination though — can clients rely on input ordering for tie-breaks?
Kai: Pagination breaks any reliance on input index across pages. Proposed contract: response includes these fields for each item: 'score' (raw), 'rank_score' (normalized), 'input_pos' (0-based index in original request), 'tie_breaker' (deterministic hash string). Tie-breaking precedence: rank_score desc -> tie_breaker asc -> input_pos asc.
Tom: That ordering makes sense. For tie_breaker, do we want hex string or base64? Keep it short so clients can sort cheaply.
Nadia: hex64 (16 bytes) is fine. Deterministic meaning derived from item id + model version + request nonce — stable for the same request, deterministic across retries.
Priya: Can you show an example response shape we can put in the spec? :+1:
Nadia: Sure — example:
```json
{
  "request_id": "r_abc123",
  "items": [
    { "id": "doc-42", "score": -2.34, "rank_score": 0.872341, "input_pos": 0, "tie_breaker": "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8" },
    { "id": "doc-11", "score": -2.34, "rank_score": 0.872341, "input_pos": 1, "tie_breaker": "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b9" }
  ]
}
```
Tom: Two follow-ups: 1) precision/format for rank_score — double but we should recommend clients round to 6 decimals for UI. 2) migration story: some older models won't emit rank_score initially.
Kai: For (1) server stores double, returns JSON number. Docs recommend 6 decimal places for display. For (2) if model doesn't provide rank_score we compute a best-effort min-max normalization on server side and set 'score_type': 'raw' or 'normalized' accordingly. Also include 'score_type' field at item-level or response-level?
Nadia: Put score_type at the item level so mixed model ensembles are explicit: e.g., "score_type": "raw" | "normalized" | "prob". That helps clients detect if rank_score is algorithmically produced.
Priya: Backwards compatibility: If client sends ?compat=1 we should keep the single 'score' field only and preserve numeric semantics. But warn that ordering might differ slightly. Can we implement a server-side shim that maps rank_score -> score when compat=1?
Tom: Yes, shim is doable. We'll need a migration checklist: API flag handling, docs update, SDK release notes. Also we should add an example under "breaking-changes" even though it's additive.
Kai: On the implementation side I'll add a deterministic tie_breaker generation in runtime: SHA256(item_id + model_version + request_nonce) truncated to 16 bytes hex. Will post PR.
Nadia: I'll draft the spec text and examples in the API docs, include the tie-break precedence and examples for pagination. Will also add a note: clients should not rely on input_pos for cross-page stability.
Priya: Can someone add a small integration test to assert stable sorting behaviour for equal rank_score items? CI-bot: make sure test runs on API contract checks.
CI-bot: Received. Please add tests under tests/api/rerank_contract/test_tie_break.py. CI will run on PR. :white_check_mark:
Tom: I'll ping when PR is up. Thanks all.
Priya: Thanks — this unblocks the frontend rollback guard. If Nadia posts the spec draft I can sign off async. :thumbsup:
